'''Mu Sigma Rho''' ('''{{lang|grc|ΜΣΡ}}''') is an American national [[honor society]] for statistics.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Mu Sigma Rho: The National Statistics Honorary Society |url=https://www.stat.purdue.edu/msr/ |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=Mu Sigma Rho: The National Statistics Honorary Society |publisher= |via=Department of Statistics, Purdue University}}</ref> It was established at [[Iowa State University]] in 1968.

==History==
Mu Sigma Rho was founded by Ted Bancroft, David Huntsberger, and Oscar Kempthorne at the Statistical Laboratory and Department of Statistics at [[Iowa State University]] in 1968.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Mu Sigma Rho at Virginia Tech |url=https://stat.vt.edu/content/stat_vt_edu/en/academics/graduate/mu-sigma-rho.html |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=College of Statistics, Virginia Tech |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":11">[http://www.jstor.org/stable/2528896 "National Statistical Honor Society Organized at Iowa State University]." ''Biometrics'', vol. 24, no. 4, 1968, p. 1053. {{jstor|2528896}}. Accessed 22 Mar. 2024.</ref> It was formed as the National Statistics Honor Society.<ref name=":2" /> Mu Sigma Rho seeks to promote and encourage scholarly activity in [[statistics]], and to recognize outstanding achievement of students, faculty, and professional statisticians in academic and non-academic institutions.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":11" />

The society was incorporated in the state of Iowa.<ref name=":11" /> Its first chapter, ''Alpha'', was established at towa State University.<ref name=":11" /> Donald K. Hotchkiss was the first president of the national society, while Eric West was the first president of the ''Alpha chapter''.<ref name=":11" />

In February 2005, the society began allowing American Statistical Association chapters to join Mu Sigma Rho as affiliate chapters.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |title=Affiliation with Mu Sigma Rho |url=https://community.amstat.org/ |access-date=2024-03-22 |website=Albuquerque Chapter of the ASA |language=en}}</ref> The allows students to join the society who attend universities and colleges that do not have a Mu Sigma Rho chapters.<ref name=":12" />

== Activities ==
Mu Sigma Rho provides outreach and professional service.<ref name="Bylaws">"[https://www.stat.purdue.edu/msr/ConstitutionAndByLaws.pdf National Articles of Incorporation, Constitution and Bylaws of Mu Sigma Rho"], (2015) ''Mu Sigma Rho:The National Statistics Honorary Society''. accessed 17 Dec 2022. via Department of Statistics, University of Purdue.</ref><ref name=":0" /> Some chapters host speakers and provide tutoring services to other students.<ref name=":2" /> The society publishes an occasional newsletter, ''The'' ''Mu Sigma Rhover''.<ref name="Bylaws" />

Mu Sigma Rho presents annual awards, including the William D. Warde Statistics Education Award and the Mu Sigma Rho Early Career Undergraduate Impact Award.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Jayawardhana |first=Ananda |date=2022-03-01 |title=Mu Sigma Rho, The National Statistics Honorary Society |url=https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2022/03/01/mu-sigma-rho-the-national-statistics-honorary-society/ |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=Amstat News |publisher=American Statistical Association |language=en-US}}</ref> The Early Career Undergraduate Impact Award is presented to a statistics faculty member for contributions to the success of undergraduate students.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Mu Sigma Rho Awards |url=https://www.stat.purdue.edu/msr/Mu_Sigma_Rho_Awards.pdf |access-date=March 21, 2024 |website=Mu Sigma Rho: The National Statistics Honorary Society |publisher= |via=Department of Statistics, Purdue University}}</ref> The Warde Statistics Education Award known as the  Statistics Education Award before 2000, is presented to a statistics instructor for excellence in the classroom and a lifetime of commitment to statistics education.<ref name=":1" /> Faculty at any academic institution in the United States are eligible; recipients do not have to work for Mu Sigma Rho member institutions.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" />  The names and photos of the winners are on the Mu Sigma Rho website.

== Membership ==
Mu Sigma Rho's membership consists of undergraduate students, graduate students, faculty, and honorary members.<ref name=":2" />

To be eligible for membership, undergraduates must have completed two years of college and eight semester hours of statistics courses, including five hours at a junior level, with a 3.40 GPA in those courses and a 3.20 GPA overall.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Mu Sigma Rho |url=https://www.elon.edu/u/academics/arts-and-sciences/mathematics-statistics/student-recognition/mu-sigma-rho/ |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=Elon University |language=en}}</ref> Graduate students seeking membership must have completed twelve semester hours with a 3.50 GPA.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Mu Sigma Rho UA |url=https://sites.google.com/math.arizona.edu/ua-mu-sigma-rho/home |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=University of Arizona |language=en-US}}</ref>
